name: Euro-area economy
summary: Eurostat confirmed euro-area Q3 GDP growth of 0.4% on 13 Nov; October composite PMI stayed above 50
state: Eurostat's estimate of 13 Nov confirmed euro-area GDP growth of 0.4% in the third quarter, with employment stable (Eurostat). S&P Global said on 5 Nov that euro-area growth slowed in October but remained consistent with GDP rising about 0.3% a quarter, with the HCOB composite PMI at a four-month low of 51.7, above 50 (S&P Global). Searches on 18 Nov found no new data; November flash PMIs are due later in the month.
for_you: Conditions are broadly stable for euro-area households and businesses, with growth positive and business surveys still in expansion.
rubric_hit: Normal: Q3 GDP +0.4% (positive) and October composite PMI 51.7 > 50

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% and employment stable in the euro area
S&P Global — Global PMI remains elevated in October but dips on heightened economic uncertainty

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
